title: SCStream is never stopped after a frame-extraction error, leaking a live screen capture
summary: `MacStreamSession::stop()` and `Drop` both use `callbacks.closed.swap(true)` as their guard, but the frame-output callback also latches `closed` on any extraction error. Once an extraction error fires, neither stop() nor Drop ever calls `stopCaptureWithCompletionHandler`, so the ScreenCaptureKit stream keeps capturing forever.
failure_scenario: A client opens a `frames` stream on a 1920x1080 display with maxFrameBytes = 1 MiB (any value >0 and <= max_stream_frame_bytes passes decode_frames validation). The first frame is 1920*1080*4 = 8.3 MB, so copy_complete_sample's `output_bytes > max_frame_bytes` check returns Err and latches `closed = true`. The consumer then tears the stream down: `stop()` sees closed==true, reports `completion(Ok(()))` and returns without calling stopCapture; Drop skips it for the same reason. ScreenCaptureKit keeps compositing and delivering frames at N fps for the rest of the process lifetime, burning GPU/CPU and leaving the macOS screen-recording indicator lit. A 6K display exceeding the 64 MiB max_stream_frame_bytes cap triggers the same path with default settings.
recommendation: Track stream-running state separately from the callback `closed` latch and always issue stopCaptureWithCompletionHandler exactly once from stop()/Drop.

title: MacFrameSource::stop() builds its Notified after the flag check and can hang forever
summary: `stop()` checks `stopped` and only then constructs `notified()`. tokio's Notified snapshots the notify_waiters counter at construction, so a `notify_waiters()` landing between the flag load and that construction is already accounted for and the future parks with no further wakeup coming.
failure_scenario: `ScreenshotCapability::invoke_stream` calls `source.request_stop()` then awaits `source.stop()`. The awaiting task loads `stopped` (false); the actor thread then runs `stopped.store(true)` + `notify_waiters()`; only afterwards does the task evaluate `control.stop_notify.notified()`, whose snapshot of num_notify_waiters_calls already includes that call, so poll_notified registers and parks. `stop()` never resolves: the frames operation never emits its terminal frame, its entry stays in NativeRuntime::streams, and finish_dispose() eventually fails with NATIVE_DISPOSE_TIMEOUT. The same crate gets this right elsewhere — native-core/src/stream.rs:53, native-core/src/runtime.rs:597 and backend/mod.rs:314 all build the Notified before checking state.
recommendation: Construct the `Notified` before reading `stopped` (or pin it and call `.enable()`), matching the pattern already used in stream.rs/runtime.rs.

title: CancellationToken::cancelled() builds its Notified too late and can miss a one-shot cancel
summary: The wait loop reads `reason()` first and only then constructs `notified()`. Because tokio's Notified snapshots the notify_waiters counter at construction and cancellation fires exactly once, a cancel landing in that window is lost permanently.
failure_scenario: An idle `frames` stream (static content, no new frames arriving) is torn down: begin_dispose() calls credit.cancel(Dispose) -> CancellationToken::cancel -> notify_waiters(). The stream task sits in `run_frame_stream` awaiting `LatestFrameSlot::next_frame`, whose `tokio::select!` arm is `cancellation.cancelled()`. That task had already read reason()==None and constructs its Notified after notify_waiters() ran, so the snapshot matches and it parks forever. Nothing publishes to the slot and nothing closes it, so the stream never terminates, `finish_dispose` returns NATIVE_DISPOSE_TIMEOUT, and the entry leaks in NativeRuntime::streams. Secondary hazard: `cancel()` stores `cancelled` before `reason`, so a concurrent `reason()` can observe cancelled==true with reason==REASON_NONE and wrongly report None.
recommendation: Build the Notified before checking reason (pin + `.enable()`), and store the reason before flipping the `cancelled` flag (or pack both into a single atomic).

title: startCapture blocks the Electron main thread on an unbounded channel recv
summary: `start_capture` is a synchronous `#[napi]` function that blocks on `ready_rx.recv()` with no timeout while a worker thread opens a cpal input stream. It is called directly from the Electron main process by voice-service.ts.
failure_scenario: apps/core-app/src/main/modules/voice/voice-service.ts:148 calls `nativeAudio.startCapture(...)` on the main process thread. If the user triggers dictation while a Bluetooth headset is (re)connecting, `default_input_device()` + `build_input_stream()` + `stream.play()` on CoreAudio can take seconds, and on first use macOS shows the microphone consent sheet before the AudioUnit starts. With no timeout on recv(), the whole Electron event loop is frozen for that duration — no IPC, no repaint, no CoreBox shortcut — and a wedged CoreAudio call hangs the app permanently.
recommendation: Use `recv_timeout` with a bounded budget and return a retryable error, or expose startCapture as an async napi function (AsyncTask/Promise).

title: Audio capture sessions are never garbage-collected, leaking threads and PCM buffers
summary: `start_capture` inserts a SessionHandle into a process-global map; entries are removed only by `stop_capture`/`cancel_capture`. There is no TTL or reaper, so any session the JS side abandons keeps its sample Vec and un-joined JoinHandle alive for the life of the process.
failure_scenario: The renderer that started dictation is closed or reloaded, or an exception in voice-service's async generator skips the stopCapture call. The capture thread self-stops at the 15 s max-duration cap and exits, but the SessionHandle stays in SESSIONS forever holding the interleaved f32 buffer (15 s x 48 kHz x 2 ch x 4 B ~= 5.8 MB) plus a never-joined thread handle. Repeated dictation attempts accumulate and there is no API to enumerate or purge orphaned sessions.
recommendation: Reap sessions whose `meta.stopped_reason` is Some once a TTL elapses, or have the capture thread drop its own entry when nothing has read it.

title: stopCapture/cancelCapture join the native capture thread from the JS thread
summary: Both synchronous napi entry points call `join_handle.join()` with no timeout. The capture thread only re-checks its stop flag every POLL_INTERVAL_MS (50 ms) and then drops the cpal stream, a blocking CoreAudio/WASAPI teardown.
failure_scenario: Every dictation stop from voice-service.ts:162/272/447 (and every abortCapture at :293) blocks the Electron main process for at least one 50 ms poll interval — `thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(POLL_INTERVAL_MS))` in capture_thread_main — plus the `drop(stream)` device teardown, after which the full downmix and WAV encode also run inline on the same thread. On a stalled audio device the teardown takes far longer and `join()` has no timeout, so the UI freezes.
recommendation: Wake the capture thread with a condvar/channel instead of a 50 ms poll, and move the join plus WAV encode off the JS thread.

title: snapshotCapture re-clones and re-encodes the whole recording on every 1.2 s poll
summary: `snapshot_capture` clones the entire accumulated interleaved buffer, downmixes all of it and re-encodes a full WAV on every call. voice-service polls it in a loop, so the work grows linearly per poll and quadratically over the session — all on the Electron main thread.
failure_scenario: apps/core-app/src/main/modules/voice/voice-service.ts:425 calls `snapshotCapture(sessionId)` every PARTIAL_INTERVAL_MS (1200 ms) until auto-stop, up to DEFAULT_MAX_DURATION_MS (15 s) — roughly 12 polls. The late polls each clone ~5.8 MB of f32 samples, allocate a ~2.9 MB mono Vec, and drive hound's per-sample `write_sample` over ~720k samples, synchronously on the main thread. Total work is O(n^2) in recording length and every poll stutters the UI during live dictation.
recommendation: Encode only the delta (as drain_capture already does) or cache the encoded prefix; at minimum move the encode off the JS thread.

title: playAudio decodes arbitrary audio synchronously on the JS thread
summary: `play_audio` is a synchronous napi function that runs the full symphonia decode loop plus a downmix on the calling (Electron main) thread before returning a playback id. Nothing caps the input size.
failure_scenario: TTS or a notification sound hands playAudio a multi-minute MP3. `decode_audio` walks every packet and accumulates all samples into a Vec<f32> (10 min stereo 44.1 kHz ~= 212 MB) on the main thread, freezing the UI for the whole decode. The inline comment justifies decoding on the calling thread so bad audio surfaces synchronously, but nothing bounds the input length.
recommendation: Cap input byte length / decoded sample count, and move the decode to the playback thread or an AsyncTask so errors surface via the returned promise.

title: compose_region decodes attachment PNGs with no working-set budget (memory blow-up)
summary: Source PNGs are decoded and retained in `decoded_sources` before any size check. Only the OUTPUT is checked against `max_static_output_pixels`; `max_static_working_set_bytes` (512 MiB) is never applied to decoded inputs, and image 0.25's per-decode default cap is 512 MiB each.
failure_scenario: A `screenshot.capture/compose` request supplies 8 attachments (MAX_ATTACHMENT_COUNT), each a ~50 KB PNG of an 11000x11000 solid-colour image. Each decode stays under image 0.25's Limits::default() max_alloc of 512 MiB so none is rejected, but all 8 RgbaImages are held simultaneously in `decoded_sources` (plus the transient copy from `into_rgba8()`), pushing the Electron main process past 4 GiB RSS and into an allocator abort — from a request payload of a few hundred kilobytes.
recommendation: Build the decoder with explicit `image::Limits` derived from limits.max_static_working_set_bytes() and accumulate decoded bytes against a running budget across sources.

title: compose rejects any request containing a non-intersecting source, making its skip branch dead
summary: The loop deliberately `continue`s past sources that do not intersect the requested rect, so their attachment ids are never inserted into `used_attachments` — but the post-loop check requires every supplied attachment to have been consumed and fails the whole request.
failure_scenario: On a 3-display setup the client freezes all three displays (one attachment each) and asks to compose a region covering only two of them. The third source hits the `continue`, so used_attachments.len() == 2 while attachments.len() == 3, and compose returns SCREENSHOT_INVALID_REGION for a perfectly valid request. The non-intersecting-source branch can therefore never succeed, and callers must pre-filter sources by intersection — a rule the wire contract never states.
recommendation: Either mark a skipped source's attachments as used, or drop the strict all-attachments-consumed check in favour of rejecting only genuinely unreferenced attachments.

title: Screenshot adapter is a OnceLock, so dispose() permanently kills the capability for the process
summary: The NapiRuntimeAdapter and its NativeRuntime live in a process-wide `OnceLock` with no reset path, while `dispose()` sets `NativeRuntime.disposed` permanently. A second carrier created after disposal handshakes successfully but every operation fails.
failure_scenario: The native-capabilities module is destroyed (module hot-reload in dev, or a module restart) and calls `nativeProtocolTransport.dispose()` -> nativeProtocolV1Dispose -> NativeRuntime::begin_dispose, which sets `disposed` forever. A newly constructed NapiCarrier from loadScreenshotCarrier() still receives a healthy server_hello (handshake never checks `disposed`) advertising screenshot.capture as available, but every invoke returns `Ok(error_response(..., transport_disposed()))`. Screenshots stay broken until the whole app restarts, and because the failure arrives as a well-formed ok=false response rather than a carrier error, no unavailable-backend fallback is triggered.
recommendation: Make the adapter re-creatable (e.g. RwLock<Option<Arc<..>>> rebuilt on the next handshake), or have `handshake` reject with TRANSPORT_DISPOSED so callers can detect the terminal state.

title: napi boundary flattens structured ProtocolError into a string, dropping category/retryable/details
summary: `to_napi_error` formats only `code: message` into a napi Error. The `category`, `retryable` and `details` fields the protocol defines and validates are discarded, so JS cannot distinguish a retryable timeout from a permanent validation failure without re-parsing the string.
failure_scenario: `NativeRuntime::open_stream` returns Err for NATIVE_BUSY (retryable: true), DUPLICATE_REQUEST_ID and CAPABILITY_NOT_FOUND (retryable: false). All three reach JS as `Error: <CODE>: <message>` with Status::GenericFailure, so protocol.js cannot tell 'busy, retry shortly' from 'capability missing, give up'. Any consumer wanting that distinction must string-split on ': ' and hardcode a retryable list, duplicating the flag ProtocolError already carries, and `details` — which validate_error explicitly permits — is unreachable from JS entirely.
recommendation: Serialize the ProtocolError to JSON and attach it to the napi Error (e.g. as `reason`) so JS reads code/category/retryable/details directly.

title: protocol.js discards every native error with bare catch blocks
summary: handshake/invoke/openStream/cancel/dispose all use `catch { throw carrierError(...) }` with no binding, so the original error object — the only place the native code and message survive — is dropped and never attached as `cause`.
failure_scenario: A stream open fails with NATIVE_BUSY because max_open_streams (16) is saturated. The napi Error carrying that code is swallowed by the bare `catch`, and the caller sees only `NativeCarrierError: CARRIER_OPEN_STREAM_FAILED / Native carrier could not open the stream` — no code, no message, no `cause` chain — so neither the retry-vs-abort decision nor any log-based diagnosis of native failures is possible. `acknowledge` (line 223) is the one method that binds the error and inspects `error.code`, proving the information is available at these sites.
recommendation: Bind the caught error and pass it through as `{ cause: error }` on NativeCarrierError, and include its `code`/`message` in safeLog.

title: request_stop silently orphans an SCStream when the macOS actor mailbox is full
summary: `MacFrameSource::request_stop` posts `Command::StopFrames` with `try_send`. On a full 16-slot mailbox it just marks the control as stopped and returns, so the ActorState entry and its live SCStream session are never torn down.
failure_scenario: The single actor thread is blocked inside `wait_for_image` (up to SYSTEM_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT = 5 s) while ACTOR_QUEUE_CAPACITY (16) refresh/capture commands queue behind it. A frames consumer disconnects and calls request_stop; try_send returns TrySendError::Full, the caller is told the stream stopped, but `ActorState::streams` still holds the MacStreamSession. ScreenCaptureKit keeps capturing that display or window at the configured fps until the entire actor shuts down.
recommendation: Retry the StopFrames command with a bounded blocking send, or keep a separate stop queue the actor drains, rather than reporting success on a dropped command.

title: Discarded ax_actor.reset() error permanently desyncs UI-element hit testing
summary: After a successful refresh the AX actor's generation is reset with `let _ = ...`, discarding BackendBusy/BackendFailed. If the reset never lands, the AX actor keeps the previous generation while the screen actor advances.
failure_scenario: The AX actor mailbox (AX_QUEUE_CAPACITY = 16) is saturated or its thread is mid-AX-call, so `submit` returns TrySendError::Full and reset() fails with SCREENSHOT_BACKEND_BUSY. The caller still sees refresh succeed with generation N while AxActorState.generation stays at N-1, so every later prepare_hit_test trips `self.generation.as_ref() != Some(&request.generation)` and returns AccessibilityFallback::UnverifiedWindow. UI-element hit testing silently degrades to window-only with no error surfaced, and the stale `elements` map (up to max_ax_elements = 512 retained AXUIElements) is never cleared.
recommendation: Propagate the reset failure (fail the refresh or mark the snapshot degraded), or let the AX actor adopt the generation carried on each request.

title: Windows with a degenerate frame are silently dropped from every content snapshot
summary: `refresh` converts SCK windows and CGWindow metadata with `filter_map(... .ok())`, discarding the reason a window failed validation. GlobalDipRect::new rejects any non-positive width/height, so such windows vanish with no diagnostic.
evidence:
let shareable_windows = system_windows
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|window| shareable_window(window, generation_number).ok())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let cg_windows = cg_windows
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|window| cg_window(window).ok())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
failure_scenario: A window is mid-creation or fully collapsed so ScreenCaptureKit reports a zero-height frame; `global_rect` -> `GlobalDipRect::new` fails with 'rectangle dimensions must be positive' and the whole window is dropped by `.ok()`. It never appears in the snapshot, `hit_test` cannot return it, and a later `capture` targeting it fails with SCREENSHOT_WINDOW_NOT_FOUND — with nothing in the logs explaining why, because the GeometryError was thrown away at the filter_map.
recommendation: Count and report dropped windows (a counter on the refresh response, or a debug log of the GeometryError) instead of discarding the Result silently.

title: Window selection ignores the configured ScreenshotLimits and hardcodes the defaults
summary: Every constructor in window_candidates.rs calls `ScreenshotLimits::default()` internally instead of accepting the limits the capability was built with, unlike the rest of the crate which threads `limits` through explicitly.
failure_scenario: `ScreenshotCapability::new(backend, limits)` and `platform_backend(limits)` both take a ScreenshotLimits, and decode_hit_test already clamps max_candidates against the configured limits — but WindowHitTestOptions::new then re-clamps against the hardcoded default of 16. The same applies to max_bundle_id_bytes / max_application_name_bytes / max_title_scalars in WindowOwner::new, ShareableWindow::new, SelfWindowPolicy::new and WindowSelectionPolicy::new. Any deployment or test constructing non-default limits gets them silently ignored for window selection while they are honoured everywhere else, so the two layers disagree about what is valid.
recommendation: Pass `ScreenshotLimits` into these constructors like the rest of the crate does instead of re-deriving the default.

title: audio.d.ts documents playAudio as throwing when the binding is unavailable; audio.js never does
summary: The declared contract says playAudio throws when the binding is unavailable, but the JS wrapper deliberately degrades to a no-op `{ playbackId: '' }` in exactly that case.
failure_scenario: A caller follows the .d.ts, wraps playAudio in try/catch to detect 'audio unavailable', gets no exception, and passes the returned `playbackId: ''` to stopPlayback. The empty id matches no entry in the playbacks map so stopPlayback is a silent no-op, and the caller believes playback started. The unavailable-binding branch is unobservable through the documented interface.
recommendation: Correct the JSDoc: it degrades to `{ playbackId: '' }` when disabled or unavailable and only throws on undecodable audio.

title: cancelCapture is typed as returning void but throws for an unknown session id
summary: `cancelCapture` is declared `: void` with no throw documented, while the Rust implementation returns Err for a missing session and audio.js forwards it unchanged. The adjacent `drainCapture` declaration documents exactly this throw, so the omission is an inconsistency inside one file.
failure_scenario: Calling cancelCapture for a session that already auto-stopped on trailing silence (so stop_capture removed it from SESSIONS) throws `session-not-found: <id>` instead of returning void. The only in-repo caller had to discover this the hard way and wrap it defensively — voice-service.ts:291-297 `abortCapture` catches with the comment 'best effort — session may already be gone'. Any new caller trusting the `: void` signature and the .d.ts's silence about throwing gets an unexpected exception on a routine abort-after-auto-stop.
recommendation: Document the throw in the .d.ts to match drainCapture, or make cancelCapture idempotent for unknown ids.

title: writeDarwinAppIcon calls a blocking *Sync native function on the JS thread
summary: The wrapper is `async` but only yields one macrotask before invoking `writeDarwinAppIconSync`, which performs the icon extraction and disk write inline on the Electron main thread.
evidence:
await new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve))
  return nativeBinding.writeDarwinAppIconSync(options)
failure_scenario: apps/core-app/src/main/service/icon-service.ts imports writeDarwinAppIcon and calls it per application while indexing. The `setImmediate` hop drains one event-loop turn, but the native call itself is fully synchronous, so each icon read (NSWorkspace icon fetch + PNG encode + file write) blocks the main process. Batch-indexing dozens of apps produces a visibly stuttering UI behind an API whose signature promises asynchrony.
recommendation: Expose an async native binding (AsyncTask/Promise) or run the sync call on a worker thread rather than hiding a sync native call behind an async signature.
